purpose: Teach: 一豊/姫路/遡る/騒がせ/無口/高台/打線/東京ドーム

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、戦国大名の、本気で、絶対、一豊、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、感心
lines.en: Sakura, your paper on the Sengoku daimyo Yamauchi Kazutoyo was really impressive. I was genuinely moved by how thoroughly you handled it.
lines.style: Warm, measured appreciation. Gentle emphasis on the daimyo's name. Steady pace, like she's reflecting aloud. A teacher giving honest praise without overdoing it.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。世界遺産の、本気で、絶対、姫路、絶対、城、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you so much. I really tried to do justice to the world heritage aspects of Himeji Castle in my research. I'm grateful for your guidance.
lines.style: Respectful, sincere gratitude. Slight lift on 'Himeji Castle'—pride in the subject matter. Steady voice, no rushing. The tone of a student who genuinely means her thanks.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 歴史を、本気で、絶対、遡る、絶対、視点、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、視野、広い、絶対、立派、絶対、本気で、感心
lines.en: The way you traced history back through different perspectives was remarkable. Your scope was really impressive—I was struck by how you built such a comprehensive view.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly surprised by her own words. Measured pace with a small pause before 'impressive.' The warmth of noticing something she didn't expect to see.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。政界を、本気で、絶対、騒がせ、絶対、た、絶対、事件、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you. I wanted to include the political upheaval from that period too. I'm really proud of how deep the research became, and I appreciate you seeing all of that.
lines.style: Earnest, a touch of quiet pride underneath. Even pacing. The slight confidence of someone who worked hard and knows it. Respectful but not deferential.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 歴史的に、本気で、絶対、無口、絶対、な、絶対、隠者、絶対、論文で、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: The way you handled the historical figure—someone known for being silent, withdrawn—that showed real insight. I was genuinely impressed by how you approached it.
lines.style: Engaged, reflective tone. Slight emphasis on 'silent, withdrawn'—acknowledging the difficulty of the subject. Warm cadence. The voice of someone seeing something click into place.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。古代の、本気で、絶対、高台、絶対、神殿、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you. I tried to look at the ancient temples and elevated sites from that era too. It was a lot of research, and I really appreciate your recognition of that effort.
lines.style: Grateful and sincere. Even, steady pacing. A hint of relief—someone who put in serious work and is glad it was seen. Quiet pride, no boasting.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: プロ野球の、本気で、絶対、打線、絶対、変遷、絶対、論文で、絶対、扱っていましたね、本気で、本当に、感心
lines.en: What surprised me was how you connected all of this to professional baseball history—the evolution of batting orders over time. That was unexpected and genuinely well-integrated.
lines.style: Engaged, slightly amused at her own observation. Slight emphasis on 'professional baseball'—acknowledging the unusual connection. Warm, curious pace, like she's still thinking about it.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。歴史と、本気で、絶対、東京ドーム、絶対、建設史、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、本当に、深い、研究、絶対、感謝
lines.en: Thank you. I wanted to bring in the history of Tokyo Dome and its construction alongside everything else. I'm really grateful that you understood what I was reaching for with all of it.
lines.style: Earnest, trailing off slightly at the end. Soft gratitude. The voice of someone opening up about an ambitious idea and being relieved it landed. Genuine and unguarded.
